page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, which positions it as a memory-optimized resource. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile characterized by moderate multi-threaded capabilities alongside weaker single-core execution. The single-core performance is rated as weak to poor, with a Geekbench single-core score of 893.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating in the bottom 25%. However, the 16 dedicated physical cores scale effectively in multi-threaded workloads, achieving average tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing, Geekbench multi-core (5757.0), and software compilation. Memory bandwidth is stable, with uncached read speeds of 75.3 GB/sec and write speeds of 53.85 GB/sec, though Passmark memory scores fall into the lower 25th percentile.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge lies in its single-threaded processing limitations and lack of local storage, which makes it less suitable for latency-sensitive single-threaded applications. Qualitatively, its dedicated core allocation and high memory density offer stable, predictable resource allocation for memory-bound workloads without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated or high-frequency compute instances. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, multi-threaded text and image processing, and moderate web serving.
